hypothesis: Let H_t(z) = integral exp(t u^2) Phi(u) exp(i z u) du be the backward heat flow of the Riemann xi function, Phi the standard weight. The de Bruijn-Newman constant Lambda is the infimum of the t for which all zeros of H_t are real, and RH is equivalent to Lambda <= 0. Rodgers and Tao proved Lambda >= 0, so RH is equivalent to Lambda = 0, and Polymath15 proved Lambda <= 0.2. The reformulation turns RH into the dynamics of the FIRST EXIT of a zero from the real axis, which is inherently a statement about one pair rather than a bulk.
falsification_criterion: LIKE THE WEIL COMPRESSION, THIS FRAMING ADMITS A NUMERICAL TEST THAT CAN REFUTE RH, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS. RH is false if and only if Lambda > 0, i.e. if and only if some H_t with t > 0 has a non-real zero. Since all zeros of H_t are real for t >= 0.2 (Polymath15) the search window for a refutation is t in (0, 0.2) -- finding a single non-real zero of H_t there would refute RH outright. Conversely, verifying that the zeros of H_t are real for t in [0, 0.2] is exactly the published computation and is NOT evidence for RH: it is consistent with Lambda = 0.2, under which RH is false. So a clean numerical result here also means 'no refutation found in this window', never 'evidence for RH'.
notes: The reason to single this framing out is sensitivity, not novelty. The de Bruijn-Newman literature is substantial and I am not claiming otherwise: Rodgers-Tao (Lambda >= 0, 2018) and Polymath15 (Lambda <= 0.2, 2019) are the established bounds and the gap is [0, 0.2]. What is worth recording is that this is the second of only two framings in this repository's scope where a finite computation has the right sensitivity to decide something -- the other being the negative eigenvalues of a finite compression of Weil's form. Every statistical framing fails the filter: Alpoge-Furman section 1.4 states that the inputs are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros, so no pair-correlation, mollifier, density or random-matrix argument can reach RH however good its constants become.
implementation_gap: Not implemented here, and not close to being implemented: evaluating H_t to the precision needed to decide the reality of its zeros in (0, 0.2) requires the Taylor expansion of xi with certified error bounds, which is interval arithmetic on high-precision coefficients -- the machinery of Polymath15, not of this repository. Recorded so the gap is visible rather than implied.
